verses.verse:
युगान्तरे तु संप्राप्ते मानवैर्लाधवेच्छया।
बंशीम् जिह्वावतीम् चक्रे कश्चिद् गीतविशारदः।।८।।
verses.text: But when another age came, some master of song, because people wanted ease, made the Jihvāvatī (fipple flute).

commentary.text: Then, in the Kali age, some convenience-seeking scientific musician made a jibbhī (fipple) in it, which made it still easier. Even children began to play it. But science holds development in one hand and destruction in the other. So the sweetness that comes into the sound on the āḍī bansī (transverse flute) through practice of the lips is, on the flute with a fipple, limited and dependent, and to some extent even harmful to health. Because it is so easy, it sometimes gets broken in children's hands.
